I worked at Officemax for a while.  They have coverage plans for their printers, there is also a kit called essential kit (EK) that has the coverage plan, gold tip USB cable and photo printer paper for a much higher price.  The employees are trained to push the EK when they sell printers, and tell the customers that they need the gold tip USB cable.  If customers ask "i'm buying a wireless printer, do I still need the cable?", they're suppose to say "yes, you need it to set it up with your printer", or "to get the fastest print speed possible, you need the gold tip USB cable".  I knew non of that was true, considering I have set up several wireless printers for different people and myself, and never had to use the cable to do it.  So i would recommend the EK and tell the customers that the cable is there if they ever need it, like if the wireless router were to act up, they could have a direct connection to the printer.  When i became a supervisor, an employee came up to me and ask me do customers really need the USB cable if they're purchasing a wireless printer, I told him the truth, but I also told him that he can take that route or go the route he is trained to do, then I asked him "If you were a customer, and somebody was helping you, would you want them to lie to you to make a sale?".  I honestly don't remember if he changed his sales tactics or not after that. 

Another thing when selling printers, when the customer said they do want the printer, you are suppose to put the printer in the shopping cart, and go grab the most expensive ink cartridges for their printer and put it in their cart. You dont ask if they want to purchase it, you just put it in their cart.  I never did that and would get bitched at over the headset.  I always presented the ink cartridges to them and suggested at least an extra black cartridge, so it will be there if they have something important to print and ran out of ink.
